items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: I know this, that they both played in Celestine's band at the same time.

ctx.x: Would it have been Chris Kelly by any chance? Do you remember? It was Guy Kelly. Was it Chris Kelly of Blue? Oh, I really,
I can't remember the names. I'm not sure. I know this, that they both played in Celestine's band at the same time. I don't know,
I don't know what Celestine was doing. It was Schatz for a while. It was Schatz Madison.

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: I have a record of Oscar Salastain's memorial record.

ctx.x: Too bad they don't put, put it out.

with FM and whatever the other is. AM. AM. Right. Well, I have one more question. I have a record of Oscar Salastain's memorial record. You remember when he went to play for President Eisenhower back in the early 50s, I think it was? John Curran was the narrator on it. And at that time, in that record, he explained something about, I think, when the Saints go marching in, where he had first heard it. Yes. And that he had played it. A woman had given him the melody, and he had played it behind a gravestone in a…

I mean, I'm scared of graveyards. Well, I've heard that recording, and I would assume that Papa Salastain, of course, was telling the truth. Of course, these things happen many times. Somebody may have asked thus and such a musician or thus and such a musician to do a similar thing, and he thinks he's the first one. It's awful hard to prove something like that. Things get invented simultaneously. You'll find that true in the theory of evolution. Right. You study any subject, and you'll find the origins of it are…
